issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Rideable.messageOnRide() to be a no-argument method returning a String (see UML and example usage in Main), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) with a String parameter and implements it accordingly in Pig and Seal. This parameter mismatch is structural and will confuse students: they will implement a no-arg messageOnRide() as described in the exercise and sample Main, but the solution uses a one-argument signature. It also makes the example usage in Main (r.messageOnRide()) incompatible with the solution's interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface and its implementations consistent with the problem statement and template. Either (A) change the solution to define Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [AnimalType] [name]", or (B) update the problem statement and template (including example usage in Main and the UML) to specify a messageOnRide(String equipment) method and adjust the examples accordingly. Preferred fix: (A) remove the 'equipment' parameter from Rideable and corresponding implementations so signatures match the exercise specification and sample Main usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Rideable.messageOnRide() method with no parameters returning a String, but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) (and implementations in Pig and Seal take a parameter). This changes the method signature and expected usage/return format, creating confusion: students will be instructed (and shown in the template Main) to call r.messageOnRide() with no argument, while the solution API requires an argument and returns a different formatted string.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable API across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to define messageOnRide() with no parameters returning String and update Pig and Seal implementations to return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) update the problem statement and template to require messageOnRide(String equipment) and adjust examples accordingly. Recommended: adopt option (A) so the solution matches the problem/template specification.
